answer: A sound anti-Sybil design counts costly, verifiable work, not accounts. Each identity must lock a small stake for a full epoch, pass a proof-of-personhood check tied to a credential that cannot be cloned cheaply, and build an attestation history. A cipher commitment binds each answer to one identity without leaking private data, while a tundra of idle lookalikes stays visible for lack of sustained activity. An attacker must pay stake and time per fake node, and a vine of linked Sybils collapses when one link fails, so faking a thousand voices costs far more than joining honestly.
